anti_overlap: fd-narrative-procgen-legibility covers prose/template quality and variety, not save-path or acceptance-criteria coverage
fd-rust-ecs-determinism-plumbing covers compile-time/borrow-checker mechanics of the gather-and-append call path, not save/load migration or cross-panel value consistency
decision_lens: Prioritizes findings where a described test or acceptance criterion does not actually exercise the code path it's meant to cover (a coverage gap masquerading as coverage) over general polish; second priority is any place where two independently-derived values (e.g. colony year shown in two places) could silently disagree.
focus: Colony-naming determinism across founding and both legacy-save load paths, cross-site consistency of colony name/year (render vs masterwork text), and whether the stated acceptance criteria actually cover the plan's rulings and constraints
name: fd-colony-worldstate-integration
persona: Apply the perspective of a live-service game systems engineer who specializes in save-file migration correctness and acceptance-criteria auditing — someone who reviews feature plans for untested load paths, cross-panel state drift, and constraints that can be violated procedurally without touching the named forbidden file.
review_areas: W-1c requires the legacy-save backfill block in BOTH load_game_from and new_from_save, but W-5's T6 (legacy_save_backfills_colony_name) only names load_game_from — does the test plan leave new_from_save's backfill path completely unverified by any of the seven named tests, despite A1 requiring only that the seven named tests pass

colony_year is computed independently in two places: render_terminal.rs's SALON OVERVIEW line (`world.day() / YEAR_LENGTH + 1`) and compose.rs's gather_composition_facts (`tick / DAY_LENGTH` then `/ YEAR_LENGTH + 1`) — are `world.day()` and `tick / DAY_LENGTH` guaranteed to agree for the same in-game moment, and if they diverge, would a masterwork's own self-reference text ever disagree with what SALON OVERVIEW displays for the same year

A5 explicitly waives a render test ('a render test is NOT required') for the one player-visible display change in the whole plan (W-1d), while W-1d's own instructions are exploratory ('if world.day() is not the accessor's real name, use the same day derivation the surrounding panel already uses') — does the acceptance criteria set leave this path effectively unverified by anything but code inspection, and is that an acceptable gap given the plan's own 'DF-artifact-grade legible' bar

The constraint list forbids modifying confluence.rs roll math, misread.rs, and the chronicle echo block, but W-3a requires new-parameter signature changes reaching into tests/confluence_rarity.rs (a file explicitly about roll-rarity fixtures) — could updating that test file's call sites to satisfy the new ColonyHistoryCtx parameter inadvertently alter which rarity-forcing branch or fixture path gets exercised, violating the spirit of 'no RNG plumbing changes' without touching a forbidden file's lines

Traceability from the four canon rulings + the constraints section to the seven named tests and seven acceptance criteria — does every ruling (density/woven, named-works-only scope, frozen-text, colony-naming-bundled) and every constraint (voice/no-em-dash, frozen text, named-works-only, verbatim templates, no closed-enum edits) map to at least one enforcing test or acceptance line, or are any left to inspection-only enforcement with no named check

mint_colony_name's fallback pool (12 STEMS x 8 CODAS = 96 combinations) versus T5's coverage (`mint_colony_name(None, &id)` twice, asserts equal/non-empty) — T5 proves determinism for one arbitrary id but not that the 96-combination space is collision-safe against existing zone/settlement name pools elsewhere in the codebase, which the plan doesn't check
success_hints: Both load_game_from and new_from_save backfill paths are exercised by name in the test plan, not just one of the two
The two independent colony-year derivations (render path and compose-gather path) are shown to originate from the same underlying day value or are explicitly reconciled

Every canon ruling and every stated constraint traces to at least one specific test or acceptance criterion, with no constraint left solely to unaided code inspection where a mechanical check was feasible
